tips.heading: Spray on moisturised skin
tips.text: Scent clings better to skin that is not dry. Put on unscented lotion first, then spray.

tips.heading: Spray clothes as well as skin
tips.text: Fabric holds fragrance longer than sweaty skin. Spray from about 15 cm away on a shirt or scarf, and check first that it won't stain.

tips.heading: Pick scents that survive the heat
tips.text: Light citrus and fresh scents tend to fade first in humid weather. Woody, amber and musky ones usually hold longer.

tips.heading: Go easy on the sprays
tips.text: Heat makes scent travel further. One or two sprays is often enough, and it keeps you pleasant in a crowded jeepney.

tips.heading: Carry a decant to reapply
tips.text: A small atomiser fits in a bag or pocket. Top up after lunch or before heading out again, instead of overspraying in the morning.

tips.heading: Spray where the skin is cooler
tips.text: Wrists, inner elbows and the back of the neck work well. Don't rub your wrists together, since that dulls the opening.

tips.heading: Keep bottles out of hot places
tips.text: A parked car or a sunny window can spoil a fragrance quickly. Store bottles in a cool, dark spot, such as a drawer or the box they came in.
